name: Barranco
brief: The old seaside resort south of Miraflores: casonas, murals, galleries and bars around the main square, and three of Lima's top tasting rooms (Central, Kjolle, Mérito) within a few blocks. Walkable, best for an afternoon that runs into dinner. 30 to 45 minutes from Centro by car.

stops.name: Puente de los Suspiros and the Bajada de Baños
stops.note: The wooden bridge over the old ravine path down to the sea; walk the bajada to the beach and back up at sunset.

stops.name: Parque Municipal de Barranco
stops.note: The main square, with the library and church; Juanito's bar and the gelato shop are on its edges.

stops.name: MATE, Museo Mario Testino
stops.note: Testino's photography in a restored casona on Pedro de Osma, a block from Central.

stops.name: Museo Pedro de Osma
stops.note: Colonial art and silver in a Republican-era mansion with gardens.

stops.name: Bars on Pedro de Osma and 28 de Julio
stops.note: Piselli's 1915 bodega, BarBarian's craft beer and a run of small bars between the square and the bridge; busiest Thursday to Saturday.

name: Miraflores
brief: Clifftop parks over the Pacific, hotels and the densest cluster of restaurants, from Maido and Mayta to the cevicherías on Avenida La Mar. Safe and easy on foot by day; most visitors stay here.

stops.name: Malecón and Parque del Amor
stops.note: The cliff path over the Costa Verde, with paragliders, the mosaic benches of Parque del Amor and Larcomar below.

stops.name: Huaca Pucllana
stops.note: A pre-Inca adobe pyramid in the middle of the district, with guided visits and a site museum.

stops.name: Parque Kennedy
stops.note: The central park and its cats, with La Lucha and Al Toke Pez a block away.

stops.name: Lugar de la Memoria
stops.note: The museum of the 1980-2000 internal conflict, on the cliff at the end of Avenida La Mar.

name: Centro
brief: The historic center: Plaza Mayor, Plaza San Martín and Jirón de la Unión between them, colonial churches and old bars like Cordano and the Gran Hotel Bolívar's. Barrio Chino is a ten-minute walk east. Best by day; take a registered taxi at night.

stops.name: Plaza Mayor
stops.note: Government Palace, cathedral and the changing of the guard at noon; Bar Cordano is on the corner behind the palace.

stops.name: San Francisco church and catacombs
stops.note: The convent's ossuary tour and library; churros across the street afterwards.

stops.name: Jirón de la Unión
stops.note: The pedestrian street between the two plazas, Republican-era facades and balconies above the shops.

stops.name: Plaza San Martín
stops.note: The 1920s square in front of the Gran Hotel Bolívar, whose bar claims one of the first pisco sours.

name: Barrio Chino
brief: Lima's Chinatown around Calle Capón, next to the Mercado Central: old Cantonese chifas, dim sum on weekend mornings, bakeries and import shops. Crowded and fine by day; keep your bag close and leave by taxi after dark.

stops.name: Calle Capón and its arch
stops.note: The pedestrian block of Jirón Ucayali under the Chinese portal, with the Wa Lok, San Joy Lao and Salón Capón chifas around it.

stops.name: Mercado Central
stops.note: The city's central market, a block from Capón: fruit, spices, and lunch counters upstairs.

name: San Isidro
brief: The business district: office towers, an old olive grove and quieter dining rooms (Astrid y Gastón, Cosme, Osso, Verbena, Chifa Titi). Pleasant for a lunch and a walk; empty on Sunday evenings.

stops.name: Bosque El Olivar
stops.note: A colonial-era olive grove turned park, a short walk from Cosme and Astrid y Gastón.

stops.name: Huaca Huallamarca
stops.note: A restored adobe pyramid with a small museum among the apartment blocks.

name: Surquillo
brief: Working district across the expressway from Miraflores: the Mercado N.º 1 ceviche stalls, Bran's anticuchos, and two small tasting counters (Piedra, Otôto).

name: Pueblo Libre
brief: A quiet older district with the Antigua Taberna Queirolo and Museo Larco; pair the two for a half day.

stops.name: Museo Larco
stops.note: Pre-Columbian collection in an 18th-century mansion with gardens and a café.

name: La Victoria
brief: A busy commercial district south of Centro (Gamarra's garment blocks) with some of the most popular local cevicherías. Go by taxi at lunch.

name: Lince
brief: A residential middle-class district between Centro and San Isidro with criollo kitchens and soup houses.

name: Chorrillos
brief: The fishing district south of Barranco, with its wharf and family cevicherías.
